bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution delays in commissioning; customer approval lags for new facilities; geopolitical volatility in export markets; battery material pricing competition
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, strategic, execution-focused; emphasizing differentiated tech, ex-China positioning, and long-term partnerships; no revenue guidance but clear intent to sustain 35-40% growth
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Liposomal iron and vitamin C show 80% higher absorption vs conventional; green chemistry reduces waste and capex vs Chinese rivals; NSS acquisition is not just revenue add but margin enhancer via vertical integration
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net Debt and Net Debt/Equity charted as FY23 Rs 72.0 Cr (0.3x), FY24 Rs 61.1 Cr (0.2x), FY25 Rs 83.4 Cr (0.2x), FY26 Rs 33.6 Cr (0.04x) - the slide is titled "Healthy Improvement in Performance with Disciplined Balance Sheet".
- FY26 return ratios given as ROCE 22.5% and ROE 19.4%; deck lists "Steady Improvement in Performance with Disciplined Balance Sheet" among its ten key value propositions.
- Expansion funding split by project: the Rs 150 Cr Greenfield from internal accruals, the ~Rs 300 Cr Dahej battery plant from internal accruals plus debt.
- MD's message states a focus on "improving capital efficiency through disciplined working capital management" with "steady progress towards our internal targets"; the historical cash flow shows changes in working capital of -112.1 (FY26), -109.0 (FY25), -77.9 (FY24) and -33.1 (FY23) Rs Cr.
- R&D spend as % of revenue from operations: FY23 0.91%, FY24 1.71%, FY25 1.96%, FY26 1.66%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Pharma/Food & Nutrition: 59% of Q3 revenue; calcium portfolio core; Europe growth accelerating with CEP certification; Specialty Ingredients: 41% of Q3 revenue; encapsulated/premixed lines growing with new wins (tortilla giant, global FMCG); NSS acquisition contributing INR17cr revenue, margins aligned to Sudeep core
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Described as a "Technology-led Specialty Ingredients manufacturer serving the Pharmaceutical, Food & Nutrition industry", founded 1989 with 3+ decades in specialty chemistries and a "Leading player in the Excipients & Mineral actives" (source: F&S Report).
- Regulatory moat claimed as "1st and Only Company in India with US-FDA Approval for Mineral Based Ingredients" and "1 of 9 Companies Globally with European CEP Certification for Calcium Carbonate".
- Also cited as "One of the Largest Producer of Food Grade Iron Phosphate" (in terms of production capacity) and "Top Exporter of Mineral Ingredients", plus "One of the Pioneers Company in India to introduce Liposomal Ingredients".
- Customer base of 1,120+ customers across ~100 countries, including 40+ blue-chip MNCs and 14 Global Fortune 500 companies; single largest customer 8%, top 5 customers 25% (as on 31st March 2026).
- Entry barriers framed as stringent regulatory processes, long development timelines, high R&D investment and risk of compliance failure - favouring incumbents with established manufacturing and regulatory capabilities.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] In May 2025 the company acquired 85.00% shareholding in NSS - Nutrition Supplies & Services (Ireland) Limited (incorporated 1977), a maker of vitamin and mineral blends (dry, water-soluble, oil-soluble, amino acid and nucleotide blends) for high-care infant nutrition and critical care; it is described as "UK & Ireland's only IMF grade premix manufacturing facility" with 7,500+ MT capacity, 200 tailored premix products and 16 years' average relationship with its top 10 customers. NSS started contributing to revenue from 22nd May 2025.
- [Regulation/supply chain] Battery materials positioning rests on a "FEOC-Compliant Supply Chain" - "Fully aligned with FEOC compliance norms, helping customers meet regulations under the US IRA & EU Critical Raw Materials Act" - and on being a "premier reliable non-Chinese supplier" as customers diversify away from China, which the deck says accounts for nearly 100% of global LFP precursor and cathode material supply.
- [Ownership history] 2015 strategic partnership with JRS Pharma, Germany; 2024 "Strategic buyback of Stake from JRS Pharma" and diversification into sustainable battery materials; listed on BSE and NSE in 2025.
- [Board] Mr. Milin Mehta appointed as an Independent Director during the quarter, bringing expertise in strategy, finance and corporate governance (note: the management slide separately labels Mr. Milin Mehta as "Non-Independent Director").
- [End-market growth] F&S-sourced market sizes with CY24-CY29F CAGRs: Global Excipients USD 10.4 Bn at ~4.7% (to USD 13.0 Bn), India Excipients USD 856 Mn at ~11.0% (to USD 1.4 Bn), Food Ingredients USD 85.0 Bn at ~6.8% (to USD 118.0 Bn), Nutritional Ingredients USD 13.6 Bn at ~7.2% (to USD 19.3 Bn), Encapsulated USD 5.5 Bn at ~8.0%, Micronutrient USD 6.9 Bn at ~7.2%, Granulated USD 277 Mn at ~7.0%, and Battery Chemicals USD 14.4 Bn at ~41.4% (to USD 115.2 Bn).

deepdive.thesis: Strong Q3FY26 growth (52% revenue, 66% PAT) driven by specialty ingredients (41% revenue) and battery-grade iron phosphate traction, with new capacity (Nandesari Greenfield, Dahej) on track to unlock scalable, high-margin volume from H2FY27; what matters is the transition from commodity excipient supplier to strategic partner in regulated global supply chains with battery materials as a multi-year growth lever.

open.item: Board of Directors recommended a final dividend of Rs 1.50 per equity share (150%) for FY 2025-26, aggregating Rs 16,94,22,937.5, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM on 4th August 2026.

Chairman flags execution risk in ramping new capacity smoothly, navigating shifting trade dynamics, earning approvals across regulated markets, and commercialising new technologies on realistic timelines as the Company enters FY 2026-27.
SAMPL's Battery Materials Plant at Dahej advanced through the year; Phase I is planned at 25,000 MT capacity for battery-grade iron phosphate (pCAM), with completion expected by Q1 2028.
Sudeep Advanced Materials broke ground at Dahej in January 2026; Phase 1 (25,000 MT) continues to progress as planned for commissioning by April 2027, within a longer-term roadmap to 1,00,000 MT.

SAMPL's Battery Materials plant at Dahej, Gujarat (spread across 80,980 sq. metres) broke ground on 23rd January 2026; Phase I capacity of 25,000 MT per annum is targeted for commissioning by Q1 FY28.

Unit 4 at Nandesari (51,200 MTPA), built at a capex of ~Rs 150 Crs largely funded through internal accruals, is undergoing customer site approvals; commercial production is expected to ramp up through the second half of FY 2026-27 and into FY 2027-28.

open.horizon: customer validation ongoing; ramp through H2 FY27 into FY28
open.item: The Nandesari greenfield facility (51,200 MT annual capacity) completed internal validation and qualification during the year and is now in the customer validation phase; commissioning was delayed due to LPG and energy supply constraints, which have since been worked through.

Management has set restoring the working capital cycle to healthier levels as a clear priority, to be achieved through sharper demand planning, leaner inventory, stronger receivables management and better supply-chain visibility.

NSS (Ireland) currently operates at roughly a third of its capacity; management views this as embedded operating leverage with significant room for growth as Sudeep India becomes its primary ingredient supplier.
Management has set out a longer-term roadmap to scale Battery Materials capacity to 1,00,000 MT over time, beyond the initial 25,000 MT Phase 1.
Ahead of Phase 1 commissioning, the Company is upgrading an existing pharma line to produce 5,000 to 7,000 MT of battery-grade material to service already-received orders.

Once fully operational, the Nandesari greenfield facility is expected to provide capacity to support growth to approximately Rs 1,000-1,200 Crs in revenue without requiring significant additional capital expenditure.

Management flags gas supply disruptions, sharp increases in phosphoric and sulphuric acid prices, and logistics pressures as challenges the Company navigated during FY 2025-26 and continues to manage.
The Company has developed battery-grade iron phosphate and plans to set up 100,000 MTPA capacity in phases from early 2027.

Despite aggressive growth capex for Nandesari and Dahej, the Company maintains a conservative debt profile, providing substantial headroom to self-fund the next leg of capacity expansion at Dahej without further dilution.

risks.note: US tariffs introduced in August 2025 led some customers to adopt a cautious approach and initially slowed procurement. Management states 50% of the US business is now tariff-exempt, and for the remaining business ~90% of the cost impact has been passed on to customers, but exposure to further trade-policy shifts remains a watch item.

Specialised segments such as clinical and infant nutrition carry high entry barriers and long regulatory approval cycles of around 4-7 years; the Company has sought to shortcut this via the NSS (Ireland) acquisition, but the underlying regulatory-timeline risk for organic expansion into new regulated markets persists.
The Company depends on a select group of customers, with the top 10 customers contributing 40.78% of revenue in FY 2024-25, creating exposure to loss of, or reduced demand from, any large account.
The Company is exposed to price fluctuations and availability risk in key raw materials including phosphoric acid and mineral calcium, which can pressure margins if not passed through to customers.
risks.risk: Raw material price and availability risk

risks.note: Inventory days increased as the Company built higher stock levels in international markets to support new long-term contracts and new warehousing in the US, Spain and the Netherlands; management expects rotation and stabilisation to improve inventory holding days in FY 2026-27, but elevated working capital remains a near-term drag.
The Company is exposed to foreign exchange fluctuations and interest-rate risk on floating-rate borrowings, managed via natural hedges, forward contracts and interest rate swaps.
risks.risk: Financial and market risk (forex / interest rate)

risks.note: Three of the Company's four legacy manufacturing facilities are located in Vadodara, Gujarat, creating exposure to regional disruptions; the Company is diversifying its footprint through the NSS facility in Ireland and the upcoming Dahej, Gujarat plant (which itself remains within the same state).
